 Bajjaria, District East Champaran, Motihari
 ... ... Opposite Party
 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Uday Bhan Singh, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Akhileshwar Dayal, A.P.P.
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Satyavrat Verma
 Oral Order
2 18-09-2023

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2.

The present application has been filed for quashing of the First Information Report of Motihari Town P.S. Case No. 327 of 2014 instituted for the offences under Sections 406, 417, 420, 327, 396 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is a widow aged about 70 years and hence, her case be considered sympathetically.
4. Learned A.P.P. for the State rebuts the said submission and submits that the Court cannot confer benediction impelled by sympathetic consideration.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.6715 of 2017(2) dt.18-09-2023 present FIR arises from a complaint which was instituted by the complainant.

It is further submitted that the alleged date of occurrence is 20.03.2013 and the complaint came to be instituted after a great delay on 29.03.2014 whereafter the present FIR was instituted as per order of the learned trial court.

It is next submitted that the complainant alleges that he came to know that accused Ambika Dutta has a plot of land at Shantipuri (Anandpuri),
Kishori Singh vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52369826/
1 Mohalla Motihari, measuring 1 Katha thus he intended to purchase 5 dhur of land for construction of house, thus, approached Ambika Dutta on 20.03.2013.

entities.text: Kishori Singh vs State Of Bihar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further alleged that Ambika Dutta informed that the land was in the name of his mother i.e. the petitioner and also showed him the documents and the price of the land was fixed at Rs.32 lakhs for 1 Katha but since the complainant only intended to purchase 5 dhur and his uncle also wanted to purchase 5 dhur of land as such for 10 dhur of land the price fixed was Rs.16 lakhs.

It is next alleged that the complainant on 05.04.2013 transferred Rs.3 lakhs from his IDBI Bank Account to the account of the petitioner through RTGS on 04.04.2013 and thereafter again transferred of Rs.3 lakhs in the account of the petitioner from his Axis bank account.
The accused persons instead of registering the land siphoned off his money nor registered the Patna High Court CR.

6. Learned A.P.P. for the State at the outset submits that from perusal of the allegation as alleged in the FIR, it would manifest that an amount of Rs.6 lakhs was transferred in the account of the petitioner in respect of a land which the complainant intended to purchase as detailed in the FIR but the accused person instead of executing the sale deed siphoned off the money of the informant which amply demonstrates that the accused persons right from the beginning had intention of cheating as the money also has not been returned or else the FIR would not have been instituted.
7.
Considering the submission of the learned A.P.P., the Court is not inclined to entertain this application.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) Kundan/-
